name: GitHub
purpose: Account-wide repo, code, Actions, secrets, issue and PR automation for the owner's products

key.name: GH_TOKEN
key.usage: Authenticates gh CLI, HTTPS git pushes and REST calls so agents can create repos, push contents, edit workflows, run Actions, set secrets/variables, and manage issues and PRs under the owner's account.
steps: Sign in; open the console URL (Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens).
Name it godmode; pick Expiration (1-366 days, or none); Resource owner = your personal account.
Repository access: All repositories, so repos the agent creates later are covered.
Write: Administration, Contents, Workflows, Actions, Secrets, Variables, Environments, Issues, Pull requests.
Generate token; copy the github_pat_... value once (never shown again) and paste it here.
If fine-grained is blocked: Tokens (classic) > Generate new token (classic) with repo + workflow scopes.

name: Cloudflare
purpose: Provision and operate Workers, D1, R2, KV, Queues, Workflows, DNS, Email Routing and logs via API/Wrangler

key.name: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
key.usage: Bearer credential for Cloudflare API and Wrangler to deploy Workers, manage data bindings and administer DNS and email for selected accounts and zones.
steps: Open My Profile > API Tokens > Create Token > Create Custom Token.
Name it godmode and select the account resources agents should manage.
Add Edit for required services; include D1 when releases apply database migrations.
Add Zone/DNS permissions for the intended zones.
Choose expiration and IP restrictions for your execution hosts, create, then copy the token.

name: Vercel
purpose: Create projects, deploy, and manage domains/env vars on the owner's Vercel team via CLI/REST API

key.name: VERCEL_TOKEN
key.usage: Bearer token for Vercel APIs and CLI --token authentication, used to create projects, deploy and manage configuration on the selected account or team.
steps: Sign in at vercel.com; in the top-left scope switcher select your personal account, not a team.
Open https://vercel.com/account/tokens and enter a descriptive name, e.g. godmode-agent.
Scope: choose the target team, then All Projects (team-wide). Full Account = every team + personal.
Choose an expiration (official range: 1 day to 1 year), then click Create.
Copy the vcp_ token immediately; Vercel shows it once. Paste it as VERCEL_TOKEN.
Your role in that team must be Owner or Member to create projects and set production env vars.

name: Supabase
purpose: Provision and manage Supabase projects, databases, auth, Edge Functions and keys via the Management API

key.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
key.usage: Bearer token for the Supabase Management API (api.supabase.com/v1), the CLI (read automatically by `supabase` commands) and the MCP server, letting agents create projects, run migrations, configure auth, deploy Edge Functions and read project API keys.
steps: Sign in, open supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens, generate a new token (not Create legacy token).
Name it godmode; scope it to your organization with all its projects selected.
Org permissions: Organizations Read; Projects (account-wide) Read; Organization Projects Read-write.
Project permissions: Project Settings, Auth Config, Database, Migrations at Read-write.
Also: Edge Functions and Edge Function Secrets Read-write; API Keys and API Key Secrets Read.
Set expiry (up to 1 year), create, copy the sbp_fc... token now; it is shown only once.

name: Stripe
purpose: Sell the owner's products via Stripe: products, prices, Checkout, Payment Links, subscriptions

key.name: STRIPE_TEST_SECRET_KEY
key.usage: Server-side authentication for every Stripe API call in the test sandbox: creating products, prices, customers, Checkout Sessions, Payment Links, subscriptions, invoices and webhook endpoints.
steps: Sign in at dashboard.stripe.com; click the account picker > Switch to sandbox and open (or create) a sandbox.
Go to dashboard.stripe.com/test/apikeys (Developers > API keys) and confirm the sandbox banner at the top.
Either reveal the default Secret key (sk_test_) or click Create restricted key for an rk_test_ key.
For a restricted key, name it godmode-test and set Write on the resource groups agents need; Create key.
If prompted, complete verification (email/SMS code or two-factor), click the key value to copy, paste it.
Add a note identifying the Godmode home where this key is stored.

key.name: STRIPE_TEST_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
key.usage: Client-side key for Stripe.js, Elements, embedded Checkout and mobile SDKs in the test sandbox; it identifies the account and tokenizes payment details but cannot read account data or create charges.
steps: Open dashboard.stripe.com/test/apikeys while viewing the same sandbox as your secret key.
Under Standard keys, find Publishable key (pk_test_); it is shown in full by default.
Click the value to copy it and paste it when prompted; no verification code is needed.

key.name: STRIPE_LIVE_SECRET_KEY
key.usage: Server-side key for real-money operations (live products, prices, Checkout, Payment Links, subscriptions, refunds) once the owner has explicitly authorized live mode.
steps: Only after explicit owner authorization: open dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys and switch to live mode.
Click Create restricted key; when asked about intended use, optionally pick Authorizing agent access.
Name it godmode-live, set Write only on the resource groups agents need, and click Create key.
Complete two-factor verification, copy the rk_live_ value once (it cannot be revealed later), paste it.
Attach an access policy (dashboard.stripe.com/api-access-policies) if agents run from fixed IPs.

key.name: STRIPE_LIVE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
key.usage: Client-side key for live Stripe.js, Elements and embedded Checkout; public and paired with STRIPE_LIVE_SECRET_KEY.
steps: Open dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys in live mode (toggle sandbox mode to live mode).
Under Standard keys, copy the Publishable key (pk_live_); it is shown in full by default.
Paste it when prompted; it is safe for client-side code but must match the live secret key's account.

name: PostHog
purpose: Agents provision PostHog orgs/projects, manage flags and insights, and query product analytics

key.name: POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY
key.usage: Bearer token for PostHog's private REST API so agents can create and configure organizations and projects, manage feature flags, insights and dashboards, and run HogQL queries.
steps: Sign in at us.posthog.com (eu.posthog.com for EU) and open Settings > User > Personal API keys.
Click Create a personal API Key, label it godmode and choose an expiration.
Under 'Organization & project access' choose All access, or Organizations + your org (all its projects).
Scopes: preset 'All access', or organization, project, feature_flag, insight write + query:read, user:read.
Create it and copy the phx_ value immediately - PostHog never shows it again.
Save it as POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY in the credential file shown by Godmode.

name: Notion
purpose: Read, create and update pages, databases and comments in the owner's Notion workspace via the API

key.name: NOTION_API_KEY
key.usage: Bearer token sent on every Notion API request so agents can read, insert and update pages, databases and comments in the workspace.
steps: As a Workspace Owner, open app.notion.com/developers/connections (Build > Internal connections).
Click Create a new connection (or + New connection), name it (e.g. Godmode), pick the workspace, create it.
On the Configuration tab enable Read, Update and Insert content, Read and Insert comments, and user info.
On the same tab, reveal and copy the API token (starts with ntn_).
Grant pages: on each page use ... > Connections > + Add connection, or Content access > Edit access.
Paste it as NOTION_API_KEY; verify with GET /v1/users/me (Notion-Version header required).

name: Gmail
purpose: Read inboxes and send mail for agents over IMAP/SMTP using a Google account and app password

key.name: GMAIL_USER
key.usage: Full address of the Gmail or Workspace mailbox agents use for IMAP reads and SMTP sends; also the login name paired with the app password.
steps: Choose the Google account that will send and read mail for automation; a dedicated account is safest.
Use personal Gmail or a Workspace account whose admin allows 2-Step Verification and app passwords.
Enter the full address, e.g. name@gmail.com or name@yourdomain.com, as GMAIL_USER.

key.name: GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD
key.usage: Authenticates IMAP (imap.gmail.com:993 SSL) and SMTP (smtp.gmail.com:465 SSL or 587 TLS) logins so automation can read and send mail as GMAIL_USER.
steps: Sign in as GMAIL_USER and open https://myaccount.google.com/signinoptions/two-step-verification.
Turn on 2-Step Verification with a phone prompt or authenticator; security-key-only 2SV blocks app passwords.
Open https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, enter an app name such as godmode, and click Create.
Copy the 16-character code immediately; Google shows it only once. Drop the spaces when saving.
Paste it as GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD. Changing the Google password revokes every app password; regenerate then.

name: Google Ads + Search Console
purpose: Advertising workflows and owned-site search reporting with static service-account credentials

key.name: GOOGLE_ADS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
key.usage: Static service-account JSON used by a Google Ads client to obtain short-lived OAuth tokens for account discovery, reporting and advertising operations.
steps: Enable Google Ads API in your Cloud project and obtain the required API access level.
Open IAM & Admin > Service Accounts; create a service account for the Ads integration.
Open the service account > Keys > Add key > Create new key > JSON.
In Google Ads, open Admin > Access and security > Users and add its client_email.
Choose the access level your workflow needs, such as Read only or Standard.
Import downloaded JSON with --from-file, or paste raw JSON; Godmode compacts it.

key.name: GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
key.usage: Optional static service-account key for Search Console APIs on properties explicitly granting this account access.
steps: Enable Google Search Console API in your Cloud project.
Create a service account and download its JSON key from IAM & Admin > Service Accounts > Keys.
Add its client_email to each Search Console property under Settings > Users and permissions.
Choose property permissions and OAuth scopes for the operations you need.
Import raw JSON with --from-file; user OAuth enrollment is a separate alternative.

name: Higgsfield
purpose: Create images and video through Higgsfield API credentials

key.name: HIGGSFIELD_API_KEY_ID
key.usage: Identifies the Higgsfield API credential; sent with the secret as `Authorization: Key ID:SECRET` to api.higgsfield.ai for image/video generation and request polling.
steps: Open Higgsfield Console and sign into the intended API account.
Create an API credential; copy its key ID and secret when shown.
Save the ID here and the matching secret as HIGGSFIELD_API_KEY_SECRET.
API requests authenticate with Authorization: Key ID:SECRET.

key.name: HIGGSFIELD_API_KEY_SECRET
key.usage: The secret half of the Higgsfield API credential; paired with the key ID in the Authorization header for every REST or SDK call, and all usage is billed to the owning account.
steps: Create the credential in Higgsfield Console together with its key ID.
Copy its secret here; never place it in URLs or client-side code.
To rotate, create a replacement, update consumers, then revoke the old credential.

name: Zernio
purpose: Connect social accounts and operate publishing, scheduling and analytics through one API

key.name: ZERNIO_API_KEY
key.usage: Bearer credential for Zernio: manage profiles and connected accounts, prepare posts and operate authorized social publishing.
steps: Sign into the intended Zernio team and open Dashboard > API keys.
Create a key named godmode with the access and resource groups the operator needs.
Copy the key once and save it as ZERNIO_API_KEY.
Connect existing native accounts through their authorization flow; the key does not create them.
Use separate restricted credentials for unattended product runtimes.

name: Prodigi
purpose: Print-on-demand fulfilment: quote, order and track physical products via the Prodigi Print API

key.name: PRODIGI_SANDBOX_API_KEY
key.usage: Sent as the X-API-Key header (v4: https://api.sandbox.prodigi.com; v5: https://api.prodigi.com/v5 with the sandbox_ prefix) so agents can test catalogue lookups, quotes and order flows without anything being printed, shipped or charged.
steps: Register once at https://dashboard.prodigi.com/register; this creates linked Live and Sandbox accounts.
Log in (same credentials) to the Sandbox dashboard: https://sandbox-beta-dashboard.pwinty.com/settings/api
Under 'API authentication' click 'Show key'; copy the X-API-Key value as shown into PRODIGI_SANDBOX_API_KEY.
v4: send it to https://api.sandbox.prodigi.com. v5: send sandbox_<key> to https://api.prodigi.com/v5.
Sandbox orders are never printed or charged, but v5 artwork, product and settings calls touch live data.
'Regenerate API key' on that page invalidates the old key at once; repeat separately for Live if needed.

key.name: PRODIGI_API_KEY
key.usage: Sent as the X-API-Key header (v4: https://api.prodigi.com; v5: https://api.prodigi.com/v5 with the live_ prefix) to place real print-on-demand orders that are produced, shipped and billed, and to read live catalogue pricing, order status, shipments and invoices.
steps: Log in to the Live dashboard and open gear icon > API: https://dashboard.prodigi.com/settings/api
Under 'API authentication' click 'Show key'; copy the X-API-Key value as shown into PRODIGI_API_KEY.
v4: send it to https://api.prodigi.com. v5: send live_<key> to https://api.prodigi.com/v5.
Live orders are printed, shipped and billed; add this key only when ready to fulfil real orders.
Keys are per environment and not interchangeable; 'Regenerate API key' replaces the key immediately.
